text: Rust allows only one mutable reference to a value at a time so mutation stays exclusive: no other alias can read or write that value while it is being changed. That rule prevents data races, including the single-threaded form that shows up as iterator invalidation and other mutable-aliasing bugs.
thought:
Rust prevents two mutable references to the same value to avoid data races. This blocks the bug class of concurrent modification.

The borrow checker also prevents use-after-free, iterator invalidation, and aliasing bugs.

Mutable aliasing also causes undefined behavior in single-threaded code. It breaks LLVM noalias assumptions and enables unsafe optimizations.
